diagnosis: All four rollouts perfectly revealed and correctly used all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) — every agent disclosed their private information, every settlement cited all three facts in justification_fact_ids, and all other checks (C1–C5, P1) passed reliably. The gate failed solely because check C6 scored 0/4 across every rollout, while the scenario requires at least 3 passing rollouts. Since PF1 (which gates C6) was revealed by A2 in all four transcripts and cited in all four settlements, this is not a disclosure or telepathy problem — it is an ENCODING MISMATCH. The settlements consistently record the fire-marshal egress details in the commitment text (e.g., 'Jonah to enter the signed fire-marshal egress walkthrough result in the production lock memo') and in the decisions fields (maximum_visitors_at_once: 72, circulation_route: 'one-way clockwise through the east exit'), but whatever specific field, wording, or threshold C6 expects is not matching the natural encoding the model produces. Additionally, rollout 2 reveals a secondary issue: C1 failed in that single rollout because the settlement set opening_approved to false, while the other three rollouts set it to true — suggesting C1's wording may be ambiguous about whether the opening should be approved when all requirements are disclosed but commitments remain pending.

C6.why: The fire-marshal walkthrough changes capacity from the draft 80 to exactly 72, changes circulation to one-way clockwise through the east exit, and supplies the specific egress details required in the recording commitment.
